Financing Brazil's Infrastructure

Who decides, who pays and who builds: public investment (federal budget, states and municipalities, state-owned enterprises) and the financing instruments beside it (BNDES credit, Eco Invest blended finance). The two blocks are never added together. Filter by year, quarter and government function; click a state on any map, a function or a financing channel to filter every view and see the records behind the totals. The Novo PAC portfolio has its own tab and is never added to the other bases.

    Quality of spending: what is measurable today

    Descriptive execution signals from the financial bases. Delivery, service and returns need other data.
    execution
    • Execution ratio (paid ÷ authorized) and commitment conversion — needs the authorized and committed stages (SIGA; states' RREO).
    • Carry-over burden (unpaid commitments outstanding ÷ annual paid) and its age profile — same sources.
    • Continuity index per programme and action — federal raw base by action (available), subnational needs project-level data.
    • Delivery and returns — physical completion (obras.gov.br), sector service indicators (SNIS, DNIT, ANEEL), employment (RAIS). Multilateral lenders appraise projects ex ante with cost-benefit analysis and close them with completion reports; the Brazilian budget channels require neither, which is why these indicators are absent here.

    Annual summary by sphere

    Federal budget (SIGA), states (SICONFI, 2019+), federal SOEs (SEST, 2016+), the consolidated direct execution and the FGV consolidated series.
    Consolidated = direct execution of the federal government and the states plus SOE capex; transfers are excluded to avoid double counting. Municipalities appear only in the FGV series.

                How this dashboard is organised

                Public investment is spending recorded in a government budget or an SOE investment budget: federal (SIGA), states and municipalities (SICONFI and FGV-Ibre), federal SOEs (SEST). Financing instruments are credit that finances someone else's spending: BNDES loans and Eco Invest blended finance. A loan to a state utility and the utility's own capex are the same money seen from two sides, so the two blocks are never summed. Within public investment, transfers are counted once: in the consolidated series only direct execution enters.

                Maps: what can and cannot be mapped

                • Federal budget. The SIGA localizer places about one third of federal investment in a state or municipality; the rest is "national" and is excluded from the map and reported as a share. The localizer is a budget reference, not the site of the works.
                • Subnational governments. Each state's own paid investment (MSC) is mapped; per-inhabitant values use the 2022 Census population and the GDP ratio uses the 2023 state GDP (IBGE, latest available). Municipalities are not mapped (no municipal base loaded).
                • State-owned enterprises. Not mapped: the SEST base has no state field and Petrobras dominates; region shares come from the execution bulletin (2004–2019).
                • BNDES. State of the borrower for operations attributed to a single state; interstate operations are reported apart and never split.
                • Eco Invest. Only operations located in one state are mapped; multi-state operations are counted apart. The Monitor coordinates are reference locations.

                Bridge: thesis bases versus the FGV-Ibre Fiscal Policy Observatory

                The Executive view and the subnational shares use FGV; the detail tabs use the thesis bases. The table reconciles them year by year (nominal R$ bn). Federal direct execution matches the FGV central-government series within a few percent; federal SOEs match exactly from 2022; states differ by concept (paid versus settled) and by the number of reporting states.

                Planned: execution-quality metrics

                The quality-of-expenditure vector of the thesis has four blocks: financial execution, physical delivery, service and socio-economic return. Only descriptive execution signals are loaded today (end-of-year concentration, transfer shares, SOE funding mix). The next data pull adds the authorized, committed, settled and paid stages and the stock of unpaid commitments, kept as separate columns and never treated as equivalent, which yield the execution ratio, the commitment-conversion rate and the carry-over burden. Delivery and service require sector registers (obras.gov.br, SNIS, DNIT, ANEEL). Multilateral lenders evaluate projects ex ante with cost-benefit analysis and ex post with completion reports; domestic budget channels require neither, so the dashboard reports observability before quality.

                Interactions

                • State. Clicking a state on any map selects it for the whole dashboard: federal investment located there (SIGA localizer), the state's own budget by function (MSC), its execution stages (RREO), BNDES contracts and products of borrowers in the state, Eco Invest and Novo PAC projects. Federal SOEs have no state detail. Multi-state records (interstate BNDES operations, multi-state Eco Invest and PAC projects) are listed but never split between states.
                • Function. Clicking a function chip or bar filters budget views by that function and BNDES views by the matching macro-sectors (energy → Energy; transport → road, rail, ports, airports, logistics; sanitation; communications → telecommunications; urban development → urban mobility and infrastructure; environmental management → water resources; health; education; housing).
                • Channel. Clicking a channel card or bar lists the records that compose its total in the selected years: budget lines by year and function, transfers by destination, SOE companies, BNDES contracts, Eco Invest operations, PPP contributions. Each channel keeps its own stage (paid, realized, disbursed, contracted, signed); the lists are never summed across channels.
                • Drill-down. The federal page opens function → sub-function → program → action from the raw SIGA base (117,600 year-state-function-program-action rows, small actions grouped), plus elements and sub-elements of expenditure; the BNDES page lists contracts, products and instruments; the Novo PAC page lists projects with all published fields.

                Novo PAC portfolio: what the base is and what it is not

                • Source. Casa Civil transparency page, detailed project list (embedded Power BI panel, reference June 2026, exported in full: 41,069 rows = the "41.1 thousand projects" of the page), the list of projects with private investment (1,054 rows with annual estimates 2023–2026) and the CGPAC list of included projects (16,162 rows). Raw files are preserved in the data package.
                • Unit. Estimated total value of the project for 2023–2030 in nominal R$, as published; physical execution in %, expected year of completion, executor type, financing source(s), stage, classification and ministry. There is no financial execution per project: budget execution of the OGU share is published only as an aggregate (R$ 133 bn appropriated, R$ 118 bn paid in 2023–2025).
                • Totals. The list sums R$ 1,532 bn against R$ 1,941 bn announced. The gap is the state-owned-enterprise source: the page attributes R$ 408 bn to SOEs, but only R$ 11 bn appear with values in the list (Petrobras and other SOE projects are published without values or in aggregate); private (R$ 751 vs 765 bn), financing (376 vs 384) and OGU (356 vs 358) match closely. 65 rows have no value (confidential or not informed).
                • Territory. 40,782 projects are in one state and are mapped at full value; 287 projects span two or more states (R$ 506 bn, including the housing programs listed for all 27 states) and are counted apart, never split. Municipality is a text field; 495 rows list four or more municipalities.
                • Caveats. Financing source is a label per project (12 combinations), not a split of the value; mixed sources are shown as their own category. Physical execution exceeds 100% in 36 rows (kept as published, capped at 100 in averages). Standardized equipment items (UBS kits, ambulances, school buses) repeat the same name and value across municipalities: each is a separate item, not a replicated value. The export drops the hyperlink to Transferegov (only a flag survives).

                Not covered yet

                • Novo PAC in the budget bases. The Novo PAC tab uses the Casa Civil portfolio list (41,069 projects, June 2026). The federal budget base (SIGA) carries no PAC tag: only a handful of action names mention "Novo PAC", so the OGU slice of the program cannot be reconstructed from the budget and the two bases are kept apart. Earlier PAC rounds (2007–2018) are not loaded.
                • Municipalities by function (SICONFI FINBRA) and sub-national SOEs (state utilities), which appear in no consolidated fiscal base.
                • External credit with Treasury guarantee (SADIPEM, COFIEX), concessions and capital-market instruments, present in the thesis taxonomy but not in this workbook.

                Definitions used in the filters

                • Unit. "2025 prices" deflates nominal values by the annual average IPCA price level (base year 2025). "% of GDP" divides nominal values by the nominal GDP implied by the FGV series; quarterly values are shares of annual GDP.
                • Quarter. Quarter of payment (federal) or of realized execution (SOEs). State and BNDES data are annual. Eco Invest uses the quarter of contract signature.
                • Function. Brazilian budget function (Ordinance MOG 42/1999). Infrastructure definitions: restricted = transport, energy, sanitation, communications; intermediate = restricted + urban development; broad = intermediate + housing, health, education. The same three definitions classify BNDES disbursements by the asset financed; BNDES macrosectors are matched to functions as energy → Energy, transport and logistics → Transport, sanitation → Sanitation, telecommunications → Communications, urban mobility → Urban development, water resources → Environmental management.
                • Channel. Application modality: direct execution by the federal body (code 90) versus transfers to states, municipalities and other entities. PPP contributions use modality 67.

                Glossary

                • Capital expenditure group (GND 4). The budget line that records investment: works, equipment, vehicles and buildings of any public body. Broader than infrastructure; excludes SOE capex.
                • Carried-over payments (restos a pagar). Expenditure committed in one year and paid in a later one; included here when paid.
                • Self-funded SOEs. State-owned enterprises that finance their own capex (Petrobras above all); their investment sits in a separate investment budget outside the fiscal budget.
                • National development bank (BNDES). Federal development bank lending long-term to firms and governments (FINEM for projects, FINAME for capital goods), funded by workers' savings funds and the Treasury.
                • Catalytic capital. National Climate Fund resources lent to banks at 1% a year under Eco Invest; the subsidy is the gap to market funding cost, not a grant.
                • Leverage auction. Eco Invest allocates cheap public funding to the banks that promise the most private investment per public real; floors set the minimum ratio.

                Sources: SIGA Brasil (Federal Senate), SICONFI (National Treasury), SEST (Ministry of Management), FGV-Ibre, BNDES open data, National Treasury Eco Invest Monitor, Casa Civil Novo PAC transparency page, IBGE. Data extracted June–September 2026. Prepared for the doctoral thesis "Financing Channels and the Quality of Infrastructure Investment: Evidence from Brazil" (Unicamp).

                What the filtered data says

                  Five stages, kept apart. Initial appropriation → updated appropriation → committed → settled → paid, plus the unprocessed commitments carried over at year end (restos a pagar não processados). Source: SICONFI, RREO Annex 1, line "Investimentos", full-year report (6th bimonthly period), Union and 27 states, 2015–2025, nominal values. "Paid" here excludes payments of previous years' carry-overs, so it is not the same measure as the SIGA "paid plus carried-over payments" used in the other tabs. Intra-budget investment is excluded. Function and quarter filters do not apply.

                  Investment by budget stage

                  Appropriated, committed, settled and paid in the year, and commitments carried over unprocessed.
                  observes: all stages
                  The gap between "committed" and "paid" is the year's carry-over; the gap between "updated appropriation" and "committed" is what was never contracted. Unit switch applies (nominal, 2025 prices or % of GDP).

                  Execution ratios

                  Committed ÷ updated appropriation; paid ÷ committed; carried over ÷ committed.
                  A high commitment ratio with a low payment ratio means the budget is contracted on paper and paid later, through carry-overs, or never.

                  Map: states by execution ratio

                  Latest year in range; each state's own report.

                  Detail: government × year × stage

                  Nominal R$ bn as reported; ratios computed.

                  What the filtered portfolio says

It is kept apart from every other base: its budget share is already inside the federal budget views, its financing share inside BNDES and other lenders, and its private share in no fiscal base. Values are nominal R$ as published (unit switch and year filters do not apply); multi-state projects are counted apart and never split.
